clue.text: Source of wealth bearing good returns, a mystery

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the reversed word holds the next piece inside it
returns tells us the word for the source of wealth is read backwards

parts.note: a mine is a rich source, of ore or of wealth generally

explanation.surface: A goldmine paying a good dividend turns out to be a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MINE into ENIM; 'bearing' puts G inside it to make ENIGM, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, something baffling: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Operation in force for train

indicators.note: in signals that one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to prise is to force something open with leverage
an act is a deed or operation

explanation.surface: A military operation in which troops are used for training.
explanation.definitionFit: To train for something is to practise it repeatedly: verbs with the same sense.

clue.text: Note cross not quite long enough

indicators.note: the word for cross falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: crotchety means bad-tempered, cross

explanation.surface: A musical note complaining that a crossed note is held too briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like part of the musical picture with 'long enough'; it is the definition, and 'cross' is an adjective, not a symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note in American usage, held for one beat.

clue.text: Run through one page man has covered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for man has covered, that is enclosed, the abbreviation for page

parts.note: a male is a man

explanation.surface: A man has covered a page of something one is running through.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or run through with something sharp: a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Grass that may bend back?

indicators.note: the wordplay asks for a word that still reads the same when bent back on itself, that is read backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A grass whose blades can bend backwards in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bend back' of a grass blade is really the word reading identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted on coastal dunes to bind the sand.

clue.text: Reddish-brown fish stock disappearing with this?

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
a ling is an elongated sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A brownish fish disappearing from the stock in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like fish stock, but it means livestock, which vanishes when thieves are at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the theft of cattle or livestock, the means by which stock disappears.

clue.text: Rule sounded fine, more peculiar people considered expendable

indicators.note: sounded means the word for rule is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
odder means stranger, more peculiar

explanation.surface: A rule that sounded fine treats eccentrics as dispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' turns CANON (rule) into the same-sounding CANNON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon fodder are soldiers or people regarded as expendable in war or some cause: an idiom.

clue.text: Gamble on this manic thief possibly clinching game

indicators.note: clinching means holding tight, so the shuffled letters enclose the game
possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A frenzied thief bets on a slot while winning a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MANIC THIEF into FITMACHINE, and 'clinching' puts RU inside after FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit machine is a British name for a slot machine, gambled on in pubs and arcades.

clue.text: Whips with which convict cuts bloke

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the convict goes inside the word for bloke

parts.note: a fella is a bloke, a man
a lag is a convict, especially an old one

explanation.surface: A prisoner lashes out at a man with whips.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagella are whip-like appendages on cells, the plural of flagellum, from the Latin for whip.

clue.text: One not yet out of bed for his breakfast?

definitions.text: One not yet out of bed for his breakfast?

parts.words: One not yet out of bed for his breakfast?
parts.note: one still sleeping, a napper, is also a smoked fish eaten at breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone still lying in bed while breakfast waits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper might be called by this name, and the same word is a smoked herring breakfast dish.

clue.text: Bum a heavy drinker

definitions.meaning: to bum is to cadge, to live off others
a person who soaks up alcohol like a bath item soaks water

explanation.surface: A tramp who is also a soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to cadge from others; a sponge is also slang for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: US city left secure

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to land something is to secure it, as a deal

explanation.surface: An American city that someone left safely.
explanation.definitionFit: Portland is a city in Oregon, and another in Maine, in the United States.

clue.text: Flipping choice, sexy photo

parts.note: on flipping a coin one calls heads or tails
hot means sexy, attractive

explanation.surface: Turning over a racy picture as one's choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A headshot is a photograph of a person's head and shoulders, as used by actors.

clue.text: Shade ahead of river in UK city

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown shade
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

explanation.surface: A shady spot in front of the river in a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Dundee stands on the Tay, not the Dee, though Scotland's other Dee flows through Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a city in eastern Scotland, part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Nation — I don't believe it welcomes Russian leader

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the exclamation encloses the next piece

parts.note: no way is an exclamation of disbelief

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Russian

explanation.surface: An incredulous nation greeting a visiting Russian head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian country, a nation of northern Europe.

clue.text: Win: great start

parts.note: to get is to win, obtain
cracking is informal British for excellent, great

explanation.surface: A victory makes a terrific beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cracking is an idiom meaning to start work promptly.

clue.text: Attacking someone personally, morph him with daemon

indicators.note: to morph is to change shape, so these letters are transformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to shape-shift a man into a demon as a personal attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hominem describes an argument that targets a person's character rather than the case they make.

clue.text: Animal that leaps from pan, or two ducks!

parts.note: a pot is a pan for cooking
taken as written
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, written O, so two give OO

explanation.surface: Something jumps out of the saucepan, or perhaps it is two ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small hopping marsupial of Australia, related to kangaroos.

clue.text: A mile's equal value? Wrong!

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that a near failure is as good as a mile
something wrong or out of order is said to be awry

explanation.surface: Puzzling over whether a mile is worth the same, then calling it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a miss is as good as a mile' says the two have equal value, so the phrase can be read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or faulty, as in something being amiss; the first sense comes from the proverb.

clue.text: Sheep positioned the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word for positioned is turned backwards

parts.note: put means placed, positioned

explanation.surface: A sheep placed facing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tup is a ram, a male sheep, in British farming usage.

clue.text: US author requiring it last

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
to linger is to last, persist

explanation.surface: An American writer needing a final word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: J D Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Went ahead with flyer for rock band

parts.note: led means went in front, went ahead
a zeppelin is an airship, a flyer

explanation.surface: An aviator went first for a heavy band.
explanation.definitionFit: Led Zeppelin was a famous English rock band formed in 1968.

clue.text: Given food to pass round, tongue possibly quivered

indicators.note: pass round means go around, so the word for given food encloses the next piece

parts.note: fed means given food
a tongue is one example of something that licks, a licker

explanation.surface: Food was handed round and a tongue trembled at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flickered means wavered or quivered unsteadily, like a flame.

clue.text: Fall down with course in writing

indicators.note: in signals the course word sits inside the writing word

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing
a lap is one circuit of a course

explanation.surface: Collapsing during a writing course.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolapse is for an organ to slip down out of place, a medical term for falling down.

clue.text: Mine is somehow topical

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that a mine is in some way topical.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal pit is a coal mine, the pit being its shaft and workings.

clue.text: Meeting where some participants are late?

definitions.text: Meeting where some participants are late?

parts.words: Meeting where some participants are late?
parts.note: late here means dead, so some at this gathering are departed spirits

explanation.surface: A meeting where some attendees arrive behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a gathering at which people try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Cold fish served up with hot worm

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the words for cold and fish are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
an eel is a fish
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Chilled fish served with a hot worm on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses C plus EEL to give LEEC, then H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking annelid worm.

clue.text: Bow put on upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word for put on is read upwards

parts.note: to don is to put on clothing

explanation.surface: A bow tie worn upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to bow the head briefly in greeting or assent.
